statements.text: Great to join Peter Sands from the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria for a global health briefing. Recent federal funding cuts are making it harder for us to save lives and put a stop to harmful diseases. I was encouraged to hear innovative AI tools are helping to fill the gap by  improving diagnoses and treatments and strengthening health outcomes — but AI is just one tool in our toolbelt. We need to both support new technologies and fund global health scientists, aid workers, and researchers to ensure we don’t undo decades of progress fighting these diseases.

Given gun violence is the leading cause of death among children and teens, we urge you to acknowledge the serious risks your AI systems may be exacerbating and to take immediate action to address them. We are particularly alarmed by reports that individuals have consulted your AI chatbots regarding carrying out criminal acts, committing suicide, or confided thoughts incompatible with the safety and welfare of themselves or others.
statements.venue: Joint letter (co-signed by Thompson, as chair of the Gun Violence Prevention Task Force) to OpenAI and Google DeepMind on chatbot safety

statements.text: As chatbots become more pertinent to society and individuals' lives, it is time to address the risks of chatbots providing hazardous information and AI-induced psychosis.
statements.venue: Joint letter text (co-signed by Thompson) to OpenAI and Google DeepMind

statements.text: Thank you, @rephuffman and everyone who attended our Petaluma town hall. It was valuable to discuss concerns around affordability, AI data centers, and the environment with our constituents. https://t.co/DyXJQySIcL

The data center craze has the potential to displace agriculture, use all of our water and generate very few jobs. So we need to be very, very careful with this and I think that we really need to pump the brakes on this overzealous effort to roll out our data centers in all of our communities.
statements.venue: Yuba-Sutter Farm Bureau candidate forum, reported by Patch

statements.text: We need local control of these decisions. If a community says no, that's it. [...] And if a community is interested, the data center needs to pay its own way. No data centers without protections for our water, electric rates and workers.

The House shouldn’t be taking  a six-week recess while AI whistleblowers are issuing serious warnings about the potential danger and weaponization of these tools. We need to vote on bipartisan safety proposals now. Speaker Johnson needs to keep the House in session so we can work to establish safeguards to protect our country.

Artificial Intelligence is advancing at an uncontrolled pace it is displacing workers, invading privacy, facilitating fraud, and causing significant dangers to our society. Congress must act and pass guardrails to address these issues. https://t.co/AsGaNn2jLO

Joined 106 colleagues in calling on Speaker Johnson to pass artificial intelligence safeguards. The United States can still lead the world in artificial intelligence while establishing reasonable guardrails that protect Americans and our national security. We must act before AI causes job losses, mass cybersecurity breaches, the development of biological or chemical weapons, or other devastating harm.

We write to urge you to immediately reconvene the House of Representatives to enable Congress to take urgent action to address catastrophic risk posed by advanced artificial intelligence. [...] Reasonable minds may disagree about precisely how Congress should regulate this rapidly evolving technology. We cannot disagree about the imperative for Congress to act.
statements.venue: Joint letter to Speaker Johnson (co-signed by Thompson), posted on campaign website

statements.text: Called on the Administration to ensure that the U.S. is leading the international effort to establish a global framework for safety guardrails on AI. Technology should work for society, not threaten us all. https://t.co/iNfFW6UsG7
